data.name: Aaidun
data.gender_notes: Aaidun is a masculine plural form used as a male name.
data.long_meaning: Aaidun (عائدون) is the Arabic masculine plural of ʿāʾid, 'one who returns', meaning 'those who return'. It shares the root ʿ-w-d with the name Ā'idah and the noun ʿawdah, 'return'.
data.spiritual_meaning: The name points to return and repentance; any spiritual reading placed on it is interpretive and labelled as such.
data.etymology: Masculine plural of Arabic ʿāʾid, from ʿāda, 'to return'.
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aaidun total 23, reducing to 5. Number 5 is traditionally associated with its own character. This is an interpretive tradition, not a factual claim.

faq.q: What does the name Aaidun mean?
faq.a: Aaidun means Those who return (plural of ʿāʾid).

faq.q: What is the origin of the name Aaidun?
What language does the name Aaidun come from?
faq.a: Aaidun is used in Arabic, Urdu.

faq.q: Is Aaidun a boy's name or a girl's name?
faq.a: Aaidun is used as a male name.

faq.q: How is Aaidun written in Arabic and Urdu?
faq.a: Aaidun is written عائدون in Arabic and عائدون in Urdu, and आइदून in Devanagari.

faq.q: What is the linguistic root of Aaidun?
faq.a: The root of Aaidun is ع-و-د (ʿ-w-d).

faq.q: What is the etymology of Aaidun?
faq.a: Masculine plural of Arabic ʿāʾid, from ʿāda, 'to return'.

faq.q: Does Aaidun appear in the Qur'an?
faq.a: Not a Qur'anic name; formed from the Arabic root ʿ-w-d.
Aaidun is the plural of ʿāʾid, 'one who returns', so it means 'those who return'.

faq.q: What is the numerology or lucky number of Aaidun?
faq.a: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aaidun total 23, reducing to 5. Number 5 is traditionally associated with its own character. This is an interpretive tradition, not a factual claim.

faq.q: What are the common spelling variants of Aaidun?
faq.a: Aaidun appears with variants and alternative spellings such as Aaidoon, Aidun.

faq.q: Which names are related to Aaidun?
faq.a: Names sharing form or root with Aaidun include Aaeedah, Aaiz.
Yes. Both come from the root ʿ-w-d: Ā'idah is the singular feminine 'returning', while ʿĀʾidūn is the masculine plural 'those who return'.

faq.q: Where is the name Aaidun used today?
faq.a: Aaidun is used in Arabic, Urdu naming communities. No verified registration statistics are published for it, so no popularity score is asserted.
